approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from task-local accepted scores. It keeps the best 64 scored survivors, draws breeding parents from three preferred score bands, and generates fresh molecules with fragment crossover and local graph mutations, including the inherited continuation and retry rules. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Candidate identity checks reject invalid, unstable or duplicate proposals. For each evaluation batch it builds a full pool and uses a Gaussian process with count-based molecular fingerprints and correlated posterior samples to choose which candidates receive scores. Every accepted score enters the complete model archive; the best surviving offspring can become parents of later generations.
approach.novelty: This control makes every eligible live survivor equally likely to breed. It keeps the original band draw as a passive diagnostic, then uses the existing member draw over the full eligible live population. The earlier frozen initial-cohort experiment stopped accepted descendants from becoming breeders. Here those descendants continue to breed under the original survival rule, so the new contrast tests the complete inherited score-quantile preference. I expect broader rank use and weaker generating parents to lower final scores, but only complete matched endpoints can establish that contribution. Support restrictions and probability weights change together; their separate effects and the value of the entire optimizer remain unresolved.

hypothesis: Replace the inherited score-quantile preference with uniform draws over every eligible member of the current live score-greedy survivor population, retaining the original band construction and band-choice draw passively, the existing member-choice call and partner-exclusion fallback, recursive accepted-offspring breeding, and active accepted-label count-GP allocation.

finding_summary.headline: Score-quantile preference contributes: uniform live breeding lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.045998.
finding_summary.insights:
This establishes positive conditional contribution of the inherited score-quantile preference while recursive feedback, greedy survival and the predictive selector remain active. It does not separate the value of restricting support from the value of weighting supported ranks. It also does not repeat the earlier fixed-initial-parent experiment or settle the value of the whole graph-evolution foundation.

The contrast separates participation from productive progress. Previously unsupported parents contributed to 1,427 evaluated offspring, of which 928 later bred. Yet strict generating-parent beats increased from 629 to 1,055 against weaker sources, while sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 203. Predictions also had lower error and higher within-batch ordering correlation on the changed evaluated distribution, despite worse endpoints. None of these selected associations establishes a causal mediator or a transferable surrogate-quality gain.

The molecular assessment finds recognizable biaryl amines and useful aromatic/carbonyl combinations alongside inherited reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry. The halogen-free carboxamide improvement and a strong carbon-bound-fluorine leader prevent treating unusual bonds or blanket chemical exclusions as the explanation. Broader parent participation therefore did not resolve chemical feasibility or ensure better endpoint search. Terminal admissions and unselected alternatives provide no unobserved descendant outcomes.
finding_summary.results:
All 106,858 Child breeding draws followed the uniform law over eligible current survivors, including partner exclusion. 53,199 draws used ranks that the inherited score bands could never choose, and 92,549 lay outside the passively drawn band. Mean selected topness was 0.500066, close to the exclusion-conditioned uniform expectation of 0.499988, versus 0.884073 under the original law on those same states. Accepted offspring continued to enter survivors and breed: 3,254 distinct offspring were later used, versus 2,401 for the Parent. All 435 accepted-label count-GP fits and full candidate pools remained active on each side.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.549672, a paired change of -0.045998, exceeding the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.063415, -0.038977 and -0.035602. Thirteen of fifteen task-seed endpoints and all five task means declined. The two exceptions were zaleplon seed 0 (+0.010604) and seed 2 (+0.020822); its seed 1 lost 0.059613. Seed-macro population deviation fell from 0.026593 to 0.019687. All three replicas completed without fallback or missing endpoints.

molecular.headline: Aryl amines and compact carbonyl rings coexist with peroxide, N-halogen and strained-ring chemistry under live-parent sampling
molecular.overall_character:
All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectories were read: 4,500 observations per node, including 4,350 optimizer proposals per node. Every supplied task and Search Seed 0, 1 and 2 is covered, with no missing listed path. The brief reports complete profile-matched pairing to n-62daf219c70a at 300 observations per task and ten-member batches. The molecules include annulated pyrrole carboxamides, a halogen-free spiro N/O-ring carboxamide, linked azaarenes and carbonyl-rich heterocycles, peroxide/azo/hypochlorite assemblies, recognizable biaryl cyclic amines, sulfur-containing polycycles, nitrogen/carbonyl cages and fluorinated dione or thiourea/hydrazone systems. Proposal ring-digit incidence spans 0.9287 to 0.9782 and aromatic-string incidence 0.8701 to 0.9621. Those are presence counters in SMILES, not counts of independent scaffolds or validation of geometry. Diversity is moderate across evaluated seed families, with substantial local series within seeds. Recognizable amines, amides, phenols and carbonyl rings are present, but unusual bond environments and crowded topology leave overall makeability questionable and drug-likeness weak. Every task has stereocentre-string and charge-string incidence 0.0 despite saturated stereogenic environments and available basic amines. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts, not computed physical properties. Raw trajectory scores are used throughout; initial observations, optimizer proposals, observed leaders, immediate survivor admissions and later reuse are distinguished.

The read-only log audit joins all 4,350 accepted offspring through pooled identity, actual posterior selection, emission and feedback to real earlier accepted parents. It checks parent score, serial, rank and identity against the corresponding live-population snapshot. Across 106,858 recorded actual parent draws, 96,539 use generated offspring. On 92,549 draws the chosen rank is outside the passively sampled legacy group, and 53,199 draws have zero recorded probability under the legacy law. Actual bands are reconstructed from actual ranks independently of passive band labels. These are participation diagnostics, not an activation or causal-mediation verdict, and passive bands are not counterfactual executed parents. The audit finds 3,254 accepted offspring later used as actual parents, distinguishing immediate admission, next-batch membership and terminal records without a later opportunity. This is the stated uniform draw over current live survivors; it is not the previous frozen-initial-cohort control or removal of the graph foundation. Retained score-greedy survival and GP allocation remain part of the stated comparison, without attribution of chemical changes to either. Direct-generation examples below do not characterize every ancestral choice, and parent beats are not substituted for matched endpoint gains. No oracle score is assigned to unselected alternatives, and fingerprint equivalence is not inferred from structural resemblance or score ties.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 24, 25 and 24 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 has an annulated pyrrolic carboxanilide with a larger unsaturated carbocycle, an O-F substituent and an N-S substituent. Its earlier N-H relative retains the same O-F liability. Seed 1 instead uses an N-H pyrrolic carboxamide, a fluorinated or brominated pyridyl group and a fluoromethyl ether on an unsaturated annulated ring; that ether has O-C-F connectivity, not O-F. Seed 2 reaches a halogen-free N-methyl carboxanilide with methylthio substitution and a spiro four-membered N/O ring written C2(N=CO2), fused into the annulated pyrrole region. The ordinary aryl amide motif is retained, but the small N/O ring and annulated unsaturation have unresolved geometry. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.1, aromatic-string incidence 0.9425 and halogen incidence 0.8805. The halogen-free leader is a counterexample to universal halogen dependence.
liabilities: Direct O-F and N-S bonds in one seed differ chemically from the carbon-bound fluorine in another seed's fluoromethyl ether.
The halogen-free leader still contains a crowded four-membered N/O ring; removing a halogen does not establish synthetic feasibility.
Large coupled relatives and expanded ring variants can lose useful score while retaining many of the same functional groups.
missing_features: The favored aryl/carboxamide context is present, but stable local alternatives to O-F and N-S chemistry are not consistently established at each leading score.
Credible geometry and specified stereochemistry for the spiro N/O ring and unsaturated annulated frameworks remain unestablished.
The highest-score fluorine deletion shows that further halogenation is not a universal missing capability; no exact absent target motif follows from the observed scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Seed leaders reach 0.40465559506276, 0.4145039882261785 and 0.4597940970593737. The seed-1 fluoro/bromo pyridyl variants tie exactly; that does not establish shared fingerprints. A 35-atom overgrown seed-2 relative scores 3.747882018472857e-08 and isolated O scores 0.0, so aromatic expansion or heteroatoms without the right context are insufficient. The final seed-2 enlarged N/O-ring relative scores 0.2526273352318435, while its recorded incumbent remains 0.4597940970593737. A particularly interpretable accepted lineage deletes aryl fluorine from the seed-2 parent at evaluation 138, score 0.4118821588754995, to produce evaluation 264 at 0.4597940970593737. That parent was actual rank 3, actual band 0 and passive band 0; the child was admitted, present next batch and later selected as a parent six times. Seed-1 evaluation 158 instead records crossover parents from evaluations 121 and 139 at actual ranks 8/band 1 and 56/outside legacy support, both with passive band 0; both are earlier accepted generated molecules. These are real lineage exposures, not proof that any band caused the endpoint. Parent endpoints are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081: positive seed-0 and seed-2 exceptions coexist with the seed-1 decrease.

per_task.generated_character: Seed leaders contain 33, 35 and 39 atoms. Seed 0 links a vinyl ester/hydroxypyridyl region, a pyrazole-like ring, an N-nitrosourea substituent and an unusually cross-linked fluorinated aromatic-labelled fragment. Seed 1 has linked phenyl, pyrazole-like and azaaryl regions with an exocyclic imine, an N-formyl chloroethyl-containing amide substituent, a methoxyalkyl group and O-S-methyl connectivity. Seed 2 combines methoxy azaheterocycles with N-O and N-O-O ring connections, an azo-linked azaarene, a lactone-containing aryl region and direct O-Cl. A close relative replaces O-Cl with carbon-bound aryl Cl but retains the peroxide-containing core. Mean SMILES length is 69.8, aromatic-string incidence 0.9161, ring-digit incidence 0.9287 and halogen incidence 0.5816. These are varied heteroaromatic/carbonyl assemblies rather than a lack of ring chemistry, but their nitroso, peroxide and hypochlorite environments substantially limit apparent synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: N-nitrosourea, direct O-Cl and N-O-O connections require specific stability scrutiny; they are not equivalent to ordinary carbon-bound halogens or ethers.
Azo/imine linkages and complex cross-linked or fused heterocycles leave geometry and molecular-state questions.
Small raw gains and repeated use of a descendant establish scored participation, not chemical desirability or mediation of the final endpoint difference.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent stable bond environments around nitroso, peroxide, N-O, O-S and O-Cl functionality while retaining useful heteroaromatic organization.
Accessible alternatives to the cross-linked aromatic-labelled fragment and peroxide-containing ring system are not established at the exact leading scores.
The near-scoring aryl chloride is a local partial alternative to O-Cl, not a demonstration that the remaining molecule is chemically validated.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. A sulfone-linked dione/enolic-chain molecule at seed 2/evaluation 69 scores 0.2888457269700333; a related sulfone assembly scores 0.29008182220256523. Thus 0.5 is not this panel's minimum, and aromatic/dione content alone does not assure a useful score. Leaders reach 0.5983092961702587, 0.6077243572172578 and 0.6016635859519408. The seed-0 accepted parent at evaluation 189 scores 0.5936362568979687; a recorded atom replacement changes its N-formyl substituent to N-nitroso in evaluation 197, with a small raw increase. Both actual and passive parent bands are 0, and the child is later reused 39 times. This is observed acceptance of a reactive environment, not evidence of improved chemical quality. Seed 2's O-Cl-to-aryl-Cl counterpart scores 0.6011284958839884, close to the 0.6016635859519408 leader while retaining other liabilities. The seed-2 leader traces to evaluation 243 at 0.599543427479295 through an insertion; the seed-1 leader traces to evaluation 287 at 0.6012049623078293 through several edits. The seed-1 leader is admitted in the terminal batch, so no later reuse is observable. Parent endpoints are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013; all are higher, but their own thione, O-F, cyanate or peroxide examples prevent equating higher score with stable chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 reaches 24-atom biaryl compounds bearing an N-propyl azetidine, a benzyl connection, an N-methylaniline and an aryl fluorine or chlorine. These are comparatively recognizable cyclic-amine and aryl functional groups without direct N-halogen bonds. Seed 1's 31-atom leader combines a larger unsaturated nitrogen ring, a benzylic chloride, halogenated aryl groups and a benzene-fused small oxygen ring bearing a thiol substituent. A 26-atom near leader instead places a primary aminoethyl group on an aryl/carbocyclic framework. Seed 2 has a 35-atom polycycle containing primary and tertiary amines, a small unsaturated nitrogen ring and an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre with multiple carbon attachments. Its leading relatives include bridged N/S rings. Mean proposal SMILES length is 58.1 and halogen incidence 0.9609. Basic amines are abundant; the main concerns are bond environment, topology and unspecified stereochemistry rather than missing nitrogen centres.
liabilities: Benzylic chloride, a small fused oxygen ring with thiol substitution and the unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre require separate chemical assessments.
Large unsaturated rings and multiply bridged N/S architectures can be synthetically demanding even when raw scores are high.
The displayed scores do not measure physical accessibility, solubility or selectivity.
missing_features: Stereochemical and conformational identity is absent for substituted azetidines, benzylic centres and complex ring junctions.
Conventional environments are not consistently preserved around sulfur and small unsaturated N/O rings, despite the comparatively ordinary strong seed-0 biaryl amines.
Protonation states are unspecified in neutral SMILES, but available basic centres are already present; the evidence does not justify simply adding another amine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An N-sulfonyl cyclic amine/ester scores 0.00016747245492913543 and a sulfur-oxide heterocycle without the leading amine arrangement scores 0.000436879169691416. Seed-0 fluoro/chloro biaryl leaders tie at 0.9970549721106309, seed 1 reaches 0.9418071243883505 and seed 2 0.9522479945873884. The alternative primary-aminoethyl seed-1 molecule scores 0.9284338471702084. Available aliphatic amines combined with aromatic organization associate with reward, without making a unique cyclic topology indispensable. The seed-0 leader is a recorded crossover of accepted evaluations 221 and 155, scores 0.9625239580995081 and 0.9442871435490201, at actual ranks 18/band 2 and 35/outside legacy support. Both passive bands are 0. The child simplifies their larger nitrogen-rich connecting regions, is immediately admitted, remains next batch and is later used 13 times. Seed-1 evaluation 296 inserts nitrogen and expands the ring relative to accepted evaluation 213, 0.815363416419986, whose actual band is 1 and passive band 0; both chemical changes accompany the gain, so a pure amine effect is not isolated. Seed-2 evaluation 294 records two replacements from accepted evaluation 281, 0.9057437746279172. The latter two leaders arrive in the terminal batch and have no later-draw opportunity. Parent endpoints are 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012, all higher. Parent beats and observed outside-support participation therefore do not establish improved benchmark search.

per_task.generated_character: Seed leaders contain 25, 29 and 33 atoms. Seed 0 is a compact N-propyl fused aromatic nitrogen framework annulated to an N-methyl/N-ethyl dicarbonyl ring. Seed 1 joins methylquinoline to a crowded bridged nitrogen/dicarbonyl cage. Seed 2 makes an ethoxy-substituted biaryl/pyrrolic assembly with a large lactone bridge and an annulated N-O-containing cyclic urea. These are distinct ways of combining aromatic regions with nitrogen and carbonyl groups. Mean SMILES length is 53.6, aromatic-string incidence 0.9621, ring-digit incidence 0.9782 and halogen incidence 0.2115. The recognizable carbonyl and aryl chemistry coexists with difficult cage or macrocyclic connectivity and unassigned saturated stereochemistry; high ring incidence does not validate these connectivities.
liabilities: The bridged nitrogen cage and large lactone closure create route and geometry questions despite familiar constituent groups.
The N-O cyclic urea and peroxide-containing low-scoring example need local stability assessment.
Very small late proposals can lose the useful combined context without replacing the higher numeric incumbent.
missing_features: The aryl/nitrogen/carbonyl combination is present, but simpler feasible connectivities preserving it at the leading scores are not consistently demonstrated.
Saturated junction stereochemistry, cage conformations and the large lactone-bridge geometry remain unresolved.
The near-tied N-methyl/N-ethyl examples show limited sensitivity in one context; they do not establish that all side chains or count features are interchangeable.

Its fluorines are carbon-bound; it has no direct N-F. Seed 1 reaches a 24-atom phenol/cyclic-hydrazone/thiourea assembly with an N-fluorinated hydrazinoethyl region and a four-membered unsaturated nitrogen ring. Seed 2 uses a 28-atom densely connected dicarbonyl polycycle with ring N-F, another N-F in the carbonyl-containing ring, an N-fluorinated hydrazine substituent and carbon-bound fluorine. The seed-0 leader appends fluorine to the alkyl end of accepted evaluation 132, score 0.5142266527956606; the actual parent is rank 8/band 1 despite passive band 0. The child is admitted, present next batch and later used 14 times. A related 26-atom fluoroalkenyl variant scores 0.5864310094984845, and neither requires direct N-F. transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c through the reproduced n-62daf219c70a baseline and is re-observed in n-a56491c332aa on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task and ten-member batches. Accepted leaders and relatives contain O-F, O-Cl, N-F, N-S, N-nitroso, peroxide and unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur environments. Direct accepted-parent joins show that such structures can be admitted and reused. Counterexamples include an ordinary biaryl cyclic amine, a halogen-free carboxamide whose fluorinated parent scores lower, a strong carbon-bound-only fluorinated dione, and a near-scoring aryl chloride alternative to O-Cl that still retains other liabilities. The chemistry is context-dependent, not uniformly reactive or uniformly conventional.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments within useful aromatic and polar frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer conventional local alternatives while preserving favorable functional relationships learned from real task-local feedback. Distinguish direct heteroatom-halogen bonds, carbon-bound halogens, N-O-C groups and peroxide links. Admission, reuse or a parent beat does not establish chemical desirability or guarantee a score benefit from filtering; these observations do not attribute the liability to uniform parent allocation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The geometry gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c via n-62daf219c70a and persists in the current matched panel as a four-membered N/O spiro ring, an unsaturated four-membered nitrogen ring, cross-linked aromatic-labelled fragments, nitrogen cages and larger lactone or N/S ring assemblies. High ring-digit incidence does not establish feasibility. Recognizable azetidine/biaryl amines and saturated fluorocyclobutyl groups are important counterexamples to a blanket claim that small rings are invalid. Some complex leaders beat their actual generating parents but remain below the matched Parent endpoint, separating local progress from benchmark outcome.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently pair representable rings with credible unsaturation geometry and feasible fused, spiro or bridged connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Assess ring size, bridge connectivity, unsaturation and molecular state in context while retaining access to ordinary small, fused and saturated rings. Explore feasible alternative connectivities preserving useful functional arrangements. Ring counts, aromatic labels and high raw scores cannot supply missing physical information; no general ring ban or causal mediation claim follows.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This identity gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and remains in the current complete panel. Every task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0 despite substituted azetidines, benzylic centres, spiro rings, fluorinated carbocycles and cages. Charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but available amines are present. These observations establish unspecified identity, not a measured penalty for any particular stereoisomer or protonation state.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic saturated centres and ring junctions remain without explicit stereochemical identity in the output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemistry when the generated constitution requires it, with exceptions for achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation, alkene geometry and tautomerism separately. No objective-specific state prescription follows, and equal raw scores or fingerprint features do not certify complete molecular identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a and has fresh evaluated and accepted-lineage evidence under the current budget. Tiny fragments and some enlarged coupled structures score poorly, while compact combinations of aromatic, amine and carbonyl regions can score well. The two positive matched endpoint exceptions coexist with decreases elsewhere; direct parent-band exposure and strict parent beats do not track endpoint sign uniformly. Distinct evaluated seed families prevent a claim of global scaffold collapse. Immediate admission, next-batch membership and later reuse are separately recorded, and terminal children have no subsequent draw opportunity.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve productive molecular context while controlling fragmentation, elaboration and dependence on close scaffold relatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted task-local evidence to preserve favorable relationships during simplification, growth and chemically independent scaffold replacement. Evaluate alternatives for both useful score and plausible chemistry without a fixed size rule. Keep active live-population choices separate from passive sampled bands, and distinguish accepted ancestry from unrealized counterfactuals. Broader parent participation or more descendants cannot by itself establish useful chemical coverage or a causal mediator of endpoint change.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

It does not separate the value of restricting support from the value of weighting supported ranks. It also does not repeat the earlier fixed-initial-parent experiment or settle the value of the whole graph-evolution foundation.

The contrast separates participation from productive progress. Previously unsupported parents contributed to 1,427 evaluated offspring, of which 928 later bred. Yet strict generating-parent beats increased from 629 to 1,055 against weaker sources, while sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 203. Predictions also had lower error and higher within-batch ordering correlation on the changed evaluated distribution, despite worse endpoints. None of these selected associations establishes a causal mediator or a transferable surrogate-quality gain.

The molecular assessment finds recognizable biaryl amines and useful aromatic/carbonyl combinations alongside inherited reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry. The halogen-free carboxamide improvement and a strong carbon-bound-fluorine leader prevent treating unusual bonds or blanket chemical exclusions as the explanation. Broader parent participation therefore did not resolve chemical feasibility or ensure better endpoint search. Terminal admissions and unselected alternatives provide no unobserved descendant outcomes.

finding_summary.headline: Score-quantile preference contributes: uniform live breeding lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.045998.
finding_summary.insights:
This establishes positive conditional contribution of the inherited score-quantile preference while recursive feedback, greedy survival and the predictive selector remain active. It does not separate the value of restricting support from the value of weighting supported ranks. It also does not repeat the earlier fixed-initial-parent experiment or settle the value of the whole graph-evolution foundation.

The contrast separates participation from productive progress. Previously unsupported parents contributed to 1,427 evaluated offspring, of which 928 later bred. Yet strict generating-parent beats increased from 629 to 1,055 against weaker sources, while sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 203. Predictions also had lower error and higher within-batch ordering correlation on the changed evaluated distribution, despite worse endpoints. None of these selected associations establishes a causal mediator or a transferable surrogate-quality gain.

The molecular assessment finds recognizable biaryl amines and useful aromatic/carbonyl combinations alongside inherited reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry. The halogen-free carboxamide improvement and a strong carbon-bound-fluorine leader prevent treating unusual bonds or blanket chemical exclusions as the explanation. Broader parent participation therefore did not resolve chemical feasibility or ensure better endpoint search. Terminal admissions and unselected alternatives provide no unobserved descendant outcomes.

All 106,858 Child breeding draws followed the uniform law over eligible current survivors, including partner exclusion. 53,199 draws used ranks that the inherited score bands could never choose, and 92,549 lay outside the passively drawn band.
